summary.headline: UCO Bank Q1 FY27 net profit rose 8% YoY to Rs 656 crore despite a Rs 1,237 crore one-time DTA charge; operating profit up 79.8% to Rs 2,810 crore.
summary.overview: UCO Bank reported Q1 FY27 with advances up 21.18% YoY to Rs 2,72,768 crore and deposits up 11.28% to Rs 3,32,315 crore. Operating profit rose 79.8% to Rs 2,810 crore, helped by Rs 1,018 crore of technical write-off recoveries, of which about Rs 800 crore is from a few accounts management does not expect to recur. Net profit was held to Rs 656 crore by total tax of Rs 1,919 crore, including a one-time Rs 1,237 crore DTA remeasurement on the shift to the new tax regime. Management said most asset-quality and margin metrics were within guidance, and that it would review credit growth guidance only after Q2.

financial_highlights.value: Rs 1,919 crore (regular ~Rs 625 crore plus one-time DTA Rs 1,237 crore)

financial_highlights.change: GNPA -55 bps YoY; NNPA -20 bps YoY
Was 54.06% last year and 52.66% in March; management expects normalised ~50%

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail advances grew 27.32% YoY. Home loans grew about 20% and vehicle loans about 65% YoY off a low base; management expects roughly 30% vehicle loan growth and 20-25% home loan growth.

segments.name: Agriculture
segments.commentary: Agriculture advances grew 30% YoY; gold loans are cited as a growth driver.

segments.name: MSME
segments.commentary: MSME advances grew 18.79% YoY; management expects 19-20% growth to continue. ECLGS sanctions stand at Rs 2,150 crore with Rs 1,700 crore disbursed.

segments.name: RAM (retail, agri, MSME)
segments.commentary: RAM advances grew 25.27% YoY and make up 64.5% of the book, within the 62-65% guidance; management aims to hold around 65%.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew about 17%, driven by working-capital limit drawdowns. The bank holds no IBPC exposure and is curtailing low-yield PSU and government lending.

guidance_outlook: Credit growth guidance kept at 12-14%, though management says it aims to exceed this; review after Q2 FY27 results. Rs 15,000 crore sanctioned pipeline awaiting disbursement.
NIM guidance 2.8-2.9%, with management aiming to stay slightly above 2.9%; yield on advances expected to hold.
Cost-to-income expected at or around 50% or below for FY27, despite Q1's 37.49%.
ROA of 0.68% annualised in Q1; management sees it near 1% by year-end as the DTA charge is a one-time item.
Credit cost to stay below the 0.75% guidance; deposit repricing largely complete, so cost of funds expected to stay stable.
Expected Credit Loss (ECL): about 60% of the estimated transition requirement already provided as buffer; remaining 40% to be built over the next 4-5 quarters before the ECL regime starts.
capex_capacity: Around 400 branches in West Bengal under five zonal offices; pan-India network of 3,421 branches.
GIFT City branch to open in the next month; all approvals in place and IT implementation in progress.
Omni-channel platform and corporate cash management service said to launch 'very soon'.
GST smart product to rise from Rs 25 lakh to Rs 1 crore ticket size; pre-qualified personal loan journey to be extended to the call centre.
Digital balance sheet of about Rs 35,000 crore at 30 June, up from Rs 25,000 crore at 31 March; 31 STP journeys live; about 70% of fixed deposits now booked digitally.
demand_pricing: Retail loan rates held steady, as they are linked to the repo rate; MCLR raised 5 bps to 8.80% in July 2026 from 8.75%.
Corporate pricing held steady; management sees demand shifting to loans as bond yields are limited.
Yield on advances was stable, moving only about 3 bps QoQ.
Competition from PSBs, private banks, RRBs and NBFCs; management did not quantify the split and sees it as market expansion.
Management reports no stress in any sector; corporate pipelines in infrastructure, renewable energy, transmission, steel and cement.

qa_highlights.question: Can management give full-year guidance on cost of funds, cost of deposits, cost-to-income, RAM and corporate advances, ROE and ROA?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of funds fell to 4.36% as deposit repricing completed; expected to stay stable. NIM 3.05% vs 2.8-2.9% guidance, aim to stay above 2.9%; yield on advances moved about 3 bps. Cost-to-income 37.49% in Q1 but flattered by about Rs 800 crore from few TWO accounts; FY27 target around or below 50%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bank shifting away from IBPC and low-yield government lending, and where is the rebalancing?
qa_highlights.answer: No IBPC exposure now. Growth comes from RAM (above 25%), with retail 27.3%, agri 30%, MSME 19%. Corporate grew about 17%; PSU and government lending being curtailed but is already very limited.

qa_highlights.question: What upside does UCO get from West Bengal's investment climate, given its Kolkata head office?
qa_highlights.answer: About 400 branches in West Bengal across five zonal offices; opportunities seen in steel, railway-related and infrastructure projects. Pan-India network of 3,421 branches.

qa_highlights.question: What would ROA have been under the old tax regime, and what are NIM, ROA and EBITDA guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: No figure given; the shift to the new regime is statutory. Management said ROA could have been above 1% excluding the Rs 1,237 crore charge, a rough estimate. ROA of 0.68% now, seen near 1% by year-end; NIM guidance 2.8-2.9%.

qa_highlights.question: Where is competition coming from (PSU, private, NBFC)?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition from PSBs, private banks, RRBs and NBFCs; management would not quantify the split and views the market as expanding. Digital balance sheet about Rs 35,000 crore at 30 June vs Rs 25,000 crore at 31 March; 70% of FDs booked digitally.

qa_highlights.question: Should the 12-14% credit growth guidance be raised given 21% actual growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance kept at 12-14% for now; the bank aims to grow above industry and will review only after Q2 FY27 results. Rs 15,000 crore sanctioned pipeline awaiting disbursement.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ECLGS sanction and disbursement, and is any MSME stress visible?
qa_highlights.answer: ECLGS sanctions about Rs 2,150 crore, of which Rs 1,700 crore disbursed, under 50% of eligible customers' loans. SMA-1 book (Rs 1 crore and above) fell to Rs 1,009 crore (0.36%) from Rs 1,125 crore (0.43%) in March; slippage 0.63%.

qa_highlights.question: How much ECL provision is already held versus the requirement?
qa_highlights.answer: Assessment done on the 1 April transition date; about 60% of the requirement already provided as buffer over and above mandatory provisions. Remaining 40% to be built over the next 4-5 quarters before ECL starts.

qa_highlights.question: Retail loan pricing trends and corporate pricing; was there JP Associates interest recovery in TWO income?
qa_highlights.answer: Retail rates held as they are repo-linked; MCLR raised 5 bps to 8.80% in July 2026. Corporate pricing held, with demand shifting to loans as bond yields limited. No interest recovery from JP Associates in interest income.

qa_highlights.question: Why did cost of deposits rise QoQ, why did fee income from loan processing fall, and what drove other commission?
qa_highlights.answer: Cost of deposits rose slightly due to reclassification of deposits and borrowings; overall cost of funds still lower. Advance-related fees fell as renewal charges are now recognised on actual basis; other commission rose on PSLC sale of about Rs 2,000 crore earning Rs 55 crore.

risks_watch: Q1 profit is flattered by about Rs 800 crore of TWO recoveries from a few accounts that management does not expect to recur; cost-to-income of 37.49% will normalise upward.
Credit growth running about 21% against 12-14% guidance; guidance review only after Q2 FY27, so the gap may widen or force a revision.
ECL transition: remaining 40% of the requirement to be provided over 4-5 quarters, a future provisioning drag.
Deposit cost rose QoQ due to reclassification; watch whether cost of funds stays at 4.36% after deposit repricing.
Retail vehicle loan growth of about 65% off a low base; management expects about 30% going forward. Concentration in RAM at 64.5% against a 62-65% band.
Corporate book growth driven by working-capital limit drawdowns; sustainability of demand and yield on the corporate book to watch.
ECLGS and MSME stress: management sees none, but the ECLGS 5.0 disbursement pace and SMA-1 trend need monitoring.
key_quotes: So, our cost of funds has come down to 4.36%.
We will review the guidance after the 2 nd Quarter numbers, because in the midterm, we can review.
As of now, we have not seen any risk from any sector.
So we can't quantify as to how much competition I am getting from the private or from the public sector.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, asset quality and profitability, while cautious on forward guidance: management kept the 12-14% credit growth and 2.8-2.9% NIM guidance and deferred any revision to after Q2. It was evasive on the ROA under the old tax regime and on the split of competition between private and public sector banks.

adds.what: GIFT City branch (new branch, approvals in place, IT implementation in progress)
Omni-channel platform and corporate cash management service launch

growth.why: Credit growth guidance is 12-14% for FY27 (midpoint 13%) against 21% actual advances growth, with management aiming to exceed it, but the call gives no capex figures and only branch and digital launches as capacity additions, so growth is supported without being clearly backed by capacity.
